allies.rationale_text: Habit-formation helps self-control shift good behavior from effortful restraint into automatic support.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Self-control is directly supported by the development of better habits' and 'Habits reduce cognitive load, freeing up the limited pool of effort available for self-control.'
allies.activation_condition: When building automatic habits reduces the cognitive load of conscious self-regulation, freeing capacity for higher-order decisions.

allies.rationale_text: Metacognitive-questioning helps self-control create the pause needed to inspect impulse before action.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Metacognition provides the overarching structure necessary for the reflective mind (System 2) to consciously monitor intuitive (System 1) decision-making.'
allies.activation_condition: When conscious monitoring of one's own thinking process is needed to exercise self-control over automatic impulses.

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias makes self-control rationalize a preferred impulse instead of examining it honestly.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Cognitive dissonance conflicts with self-control, which requires the discipline to identify and reconcile disconfirming evidence and scrutinize one's own models.'
antagonists.activation_condition: When the brain's model-defending behavior resists the objective self-assessment necessary for genuine self-control.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Self-control conflicts with flow when deliberate self-monitoring interrupts the automatic absorption that flow states require.
structured_tensions.source_quote: self-control conflicts with flow (flow) when deliberate self-monitoring interrupts the automatic absorption that flow states require.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Self-control conflicts with incentives when extrinsic incentive structures undermine the intrinsic self-regulation that self-control develops.
structured_tensions.source_quote: self-control conflicts with incentives (incentives) when extrinsic incentive structures undermine the intrinsic self-regulation that self-control develops.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. habit-formation 0.90 ('directly supported'), metacognitive-questioning 0.90 ('overarching structure'). confirmation-bias antagonist at 0.80. Canonical also mentions first-principles-thinking and emotional-intelligence as allies.
